changed.S2-R30: Archive and Delete ask first. "Archive \<tier\>?" (or "Delete \<tier\>?") names, one per line, each tier whose prices change because it follows this one through Same as previous tier: "These tiers price the same as \<tier\> and will follow \<tier before it\> instead:". After the list, Archive says "Parts already on work orders keep their prices." and Delete says "This can't be undone." (a tier that can be deleted never priced a part, S2-R8). Buttons: Cancel and Archive (or Delete). The list names tiers only, never matrices: every tier that follows this one in any matrix or side, directly or through another tier that follows it. If no tier follows it, the question is just "Archive \<tier\>?" or "Delete \<tier\>?" with its own last line. A tier with customers on it is blocked first (S2-R7).
changed.S2-R28: Clicking an active or archived tier's row on the Tiers list opens its page on the Pricing tab, never a dialog, with the breadcrumb Pricing › Tiers › \<tier\>, also when opened from a link or bookmark. The tier's name is the page title, renamed in place and saved at once. Coming back keeps the list's filter and page (S2-R14).
changed.S3-R26: Breadcrumbs, with no separate Back link, show where the page was opened from: Pricing › Matrices › \<matrix\>; Categories › \<category\> › \<matrix\> from a category (Uncategorized included); Pricing › Tiers › \<tier\> › \<matrix\> from a tier. Opened from a link or bookmark, the breadcrumb is Pricing › Matrices › \<matrix\>. Breadcrumbs start at the Settings page the user is on, never at Settings: the Settings side menu is always shown, and a Settings crumb would open Organization settings.
changed.S3-R13: Categories are assigned to a matrix from the matrix page's Categories line, with a multi-select category picker with search and Select all, and from a category's page with its matrix picker (S7-R9). A category on another matrix shows "Now: \<matrix\>" beside it; picking it moves it to this matrix when the matrix is saved. A category removed from the line moves to the General Matrix when the matrix is saved. Uncategorized isn't listed; it always uses the General Matrix. The Categories line can be changed only while the matrix is in Edit, or on a new matrix. Picked categories show on the line at once; their parts are priced by this matrix only after Save (Create Matrix on a new matrix), and Cancel puts them back.
changed.S3-R16: Ranges are entered by their end. The first range starts at $0.00; each later range starts $0.01 above the end of the range before it ("$25.01 to \[end\]"), so ranges never overlap or leave a gap. The first range always starts at $0.00 and the last has no end ("$10,000.01 and up"). Neither can be removed, so every cost is covered. Add Range adds a range before the last one.
changed.S3-R32: Each range between the first and the last has a delete button at its left (tooltip "Remove this range"), lined up down the grid. A matrix with one or two ranges has none. Removing a range merges it into the range above, which takes its end.
changed.S3-R12: Only a grid Save asks Change All: saving the grid of a matrix used by more than one category asks it (S4-R16). The General Matrix never asks; it confirms instead (S4-R18). A change to Default's rules also names the tiers that price from Default (S4-R30). Renaming and turning the Part Sale switch on save without asking; categories save with the grid (S3-R13); turning it off asks first, because it deletes that side's rules (S3-R27). Otherwise, a matrix used by one category, or by none, saves without asking.
changed.S4-R4: Edit turns every cell editable. An edit bar shows "No changes yet" or "\<n\> changes", with Cancel and Save and no other button. A new matrix has Cancel and Create Matrix in the page head instead. The count is what the user edited, measured against the last saved version, so a value changed and then changed back doesn't count: each cell they changed whose value now differs, each range end that differs, each range added or removed, and each column whose rule type differs counts as one change. For example, switching a 3-range column to % Off counts 1 change (its boxes start empty, S4-R7); typing a value in each of its boxes makes 4. Gray auto-filled values and cells that change only because they follow another column (Same as previous tier) don't count. Nothing changes until Save (S3-R25).
changed.S4-R12: Save validates the grid (S3-R6), then saves every column at once, after the question in S4-R16 or the confirmation in S4-R18 where they apply. The success toast reads "\<matrix\> saved" with what changed and "Parts already on work orders keep their prices.", for example "1 change: Tier 5 is 28% margin."; changes are counted as in S4-R4. Each tier's change reads one of three ways. One rule and value in every range: "Tier 5 is 28% margin." The same rule type with a different value per range: "Tier 5 is" and one bullet per range ("$0.00 to $25.00: 35% margin"). More than one rule type: "Tier 5 is multiple rules" and one bullet per type ("+ $", "Margin %"). Each tier counts as one of the three changes named before "and \<n\> more". It names up to three changes, then "and \<n\> more", for example "3 changes: Tier 5 is 28% margin; Default is 35% markup; 1 range added." Gray auto-filled ranges are saved but not counted, so a save can change more ranges than the count names. The grid returns to view.
changed.S6-R1: Settings › Pricing › Matrices lists every matrix with Matrix, Status, Categories, Tiers, Work Order Matrix (Default's rules in short) and Part Sale Matrix (its rules in short when the matrix has separate Part Sale pricing, otherwise "Same as work orders"). Status is Active or Inactive (S3-R28), with "No categories use this matrix" on hover for Inactive.
changed.S7-R6: Clicking anywhere on a category's row opens its page, never a dialog, with the breadcrumb Categories › \<category\>. The page has its name, renamed in place; its Pricing Matrix picker; QuickBooks Products and Services (only when QuickBooks is connected, as today); Tax Exempt; New Matrix; Delete, in the page's ⋯ menu (S8-R8); then the matrix's tier grid, read-only, with no simulator. Every field today's Edit Category has stays on the page. Edit works as S7-R13 says.
changed.S8-R10: New Category on the Categories page opens a New Category page: a name, a Pricing Matrix (the General Matrix unless another is picked), QuickBooks Products and Services (only when QuickBooks is connected, as today) and Tax Exempt, with the matrix's grid, read-only. A new category is priced for every tier from the start. It has Cancel and Create Category in the page head, like New Tier and New Matrix; nothing is created until Create Category (S19-R14).
changed.S8-R4: Uncategorized is a system category. It can't be renamed, deleted or edited, and always uses the General Matrix; no action changes its matrix. Its page is read-only: no rename and no Delete, and its Pricing Matrix and Tax Exempt show grayed and can't be changed. Only QuickBooks Products and Services can be changed (when QuickBooks is connected, as today), so a client can book Uncategorized to a specific P&L account. Its Edit is grayed with a link to the General Matrix, like any category on a shared matrix (S7-R13).
changed.S9-R9: A tier's Customers tab (the customers on the tier) has: - search by customer name; - a channel filter (Work orders, Part Sales, Both): Work orders lists customers on the tier for work orders only, Part Sales for Part Sales only, and Both for both, so each customer matches one option; - sorting by customer name, A to Z by default, and a sortable channel column, with ties broken by customer name; - 50 customers a page. Its search, filters, sort and page are kept when the user comes back.
changed.S10-R14: A work order or Part Sale keeps the tier its customer had for that channel when it was made, even if that tier is archived later. Every part added to it is priced by that tier's current rules; receiving follows S11-R9. A work order or Part Sale already open on release day was made before tiers, so it keeps Default for both channels, whatever tier its customer is later put on; to use the customer's tier, the advisor splits the lines onto a new work order or Part Sale (S11-E6). Moving the customer to another tier affects only work orders and Part Sales made afterwards, or made by splitting (S11-E6). Changing the customer on a work order or Part Sale doesn't change its tier either: new parts keep being priced by the tier it was made with (S14-R3). Adding a line to a work order whose invoice is sent or paid puts it on a new work order, as today. That work order is new, so its parts are priced by the customer's current tier.
changed.S12-R2: Hovering the price on desktop, or tapping it on a tablet, opens the price details. With the cursor in the price box, Alt+Down opens them; typing still edits the price. They show: - the pricing source; - the tier name; - the matrix, its side (Work Order Matrix or Part Sale Matrix) and the rule (cost range and calculation); on a Part Sale whose matrix has no separate Part Sale pricing, the side reads "Same as work orders"; - the cost used; - the sell price; - when it was priced; - for % Off or $ Off, the Default price it was taken from; - where the part came from: "Inventory, bin \<bin\>" for an inventory part (today the part number's hover shows "Inventory" with no bin), or "\<vendor\> - \<vendor bill #\>" for a special-order part, as the part number's hover shows today. A part with neither, such as a quick-added part with no vendor, has no line for it. Focus returns to the price when they close.
changed.S19-R15: The new pages show no explanatory text or help banners. Explanations (cost ranges, how a price is found, the Part Sale switch) sit in short info-icon tooltips beside the item they explain, one or two plain sentences that never repeat the label. Tier names have no tooltip. The one exception is the shared-matrix line above a category's grid (S7-R15).
changed.S19-R23: Each save makes one Audit Log entry on the log of what was saved, summing up everything that save changed, and nothing is logged for edits that weren't saved. For example, one matrix save that adds a range and sets its rules reads "1 range added; rules set for Default and 5 tiers". Set Rule makes one entry on the tier's log ("Rule set in 7 matrices") and one on each matrix it changed; Undo does the same. A bulk Manage Customers save makes one entry on the tier's log ("3 customers added, 1 removed"). A category delete makes one entry on the Categories list's log, with the number of parts and lines moved. A rule-type change and the values entered after it are both recorded, for example "Tier 5: rule type Margin % → % Off; 3 range values changed".

new.S19-R24: Columns and fields keep their place and width when a screen changes state: a row opening or closing, a search narrowing a list, an empty list, a filter chip changing, the Add Part row opening, or a page switching between view and edit. Nothing moves sideways or down.
